alignments.note: The negative indefinite carries the clause's negation, 'no man'; rule 17's generic-noun clause heads it on 'no' rather than on the supplied 'man'.
The second negative is rendered non-negatively as 'anything', so under rule 69 it cannot carry the negation and takes only that word; the negation stays on s001.
εἰ μή rendered by the single word 'save' is one indivisible unit under rule 39, headed on the first particle.
Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive, which English spells with no word of its own (rule 61); no preposition governs it, so the infinitival 'to' is the verb's own helper.
Infinitive with its marker as a rule 7 helper.
Reciprocal rendered by the two-word idiom; rule 83 heads it on 'another', the word realizing the ἄλλος lexeme.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun only (rule 32).
Participle carries the relativizer and the finite verb.
No source word stands to take the supplied possessive, so the article itself takes 'his' under rule 20's second arm.
Substantival adjective rendered 'neighbor'; the ASV's own note records the Greek as 'the other'.
Perfect indicative with its auxiliary; head on the lexical verb under rule 9.
Anarthrous noun with the supplied determiner as a rule 51 helper.

review_notes: The variant unit is underdetermined with the base compatible; no textual decision is made in the alignment (rule 12).
s001/s002 turn on rule 69: the ASV writes the negation in 'no man' and renders μηδέν positively, so neither negator is emptied.
